record.paper_title: Addition Machines, Automatic Functions and Open Problems of Floyd and Knuth
record.context_brief: sub-bound sorting of positive integers on addition machines
record.original_question: For an integer addition machine, given an arbitrary sequence of positive integers q_1, q_2, ..., q_m, can the machine sort the sequence in o((m + log(q_1 q_2 ... q_m)) log m) steps? A complete resolution should answer the asymptotic-improvement question for all common definitions of multivariate little-o, since the maximum-based convention gives a negative answer but alternative conventions remain only partially resolved.

evidence.quote: (4) Can an integer addition machine sort an arbitrary sequence of positive integers <q1, q2, . . . , qm> in o((m + log(q1 * q2 * . . . * qm) log m) steps?
Open Problem (4) is answered "no" when one bases the Little Oh Calculus on version (a) which is the one on Wikipedia
Thus these two problems are only partially solved and would be completely solved only when they are answered for all common versions of the multivariate Oh Calculus

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An integer addition machine is a register machine whose registers store integers and whose primitive operations are: (i) loading the constants 0 and 1 into a register, (ii) copying a register, (iii) computing the sum or difference of two registers and storing the result in a register, and (iv) conditional branching based on comparisons (=, <) between two registers. The "number of steps" of a computation is the total number of such primitive operations executed.

Given an input sequence of positive integers q_1, q_2, …, q_m (presented in m designated registers), the machine is said to sort the sequence if it produces in m output registers a permutation of q_1, …, q_m in non-decreasing order. Let log denote the base-2 logarithm. Define
   T(m; q_1, …, q_m) := (m + log(q_1 · q_2 · … · q_m)) · log m.

For two positive functions f, g of the multivariate input (m; q_1, …, q_m), say that f(m; q_1, …, q_m) = o(g(m; q_1, …, q_m)) under a chosen convention of multivariate little-o (for example: (a) f/g → 0 as max(m, q_1, …, q_m) → ∞; (b) f/g → 0 as min(m, q_1, …, q_m) → ∞; or any other standard convention).

Question: Does there exist an integer addition machine which, on every input sequence q_1, q_2, …, q_m of positive integers, sorts the sequence in a number of steps that is
   o((m + log(q_1 · q_2 · … · q_m)) · log m)?
Resolve this for each of the common conventions of multivariate little-o (it is known that under convention (a) the answer is negative; the other conventions are to be settled).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is one of the open problems of Floyd and Knuth concerning integer addition machines. Recent work establishes a negative answer under the "max-based" version of multivariate little-o (the Wikipedia convention), but the question remains unresolved under other standard conventions of multivariate little-o, so it is only partially solved.
